annotations.title: One-call valuation brief: intrinsic value, margin of safety, verdict, guru holders

description: Call this first when asked whether a listed company looks cheap or expensive, what it is worth, or which well-known investors own it: one call returns the intrinsic value per share (with each valuation method as an input), the owner-earnings value, the margin of safety against the current price, a deterministic verdict sentence about where the price sits against our value range, the top tracked 13F holders and their last move, and the company profile. Every number carries its unit, period, as-of date and a sec.gov source link, and `checks` lists the sanity checks it passed. A value built from statements filed in another currency and converted to USD carries `fx` (original currency, rate, rate date) and passes `currency_consistent`; when the currency is not known the flag `currency_unverified` says the check did not run. If the valuation fails a check (for example an intrinsic value more than 20x the price, or statements left in a currency other than the USD price), the valuation figures are withheld, `withheld` is true, `checks.failed` names the check, and the call is not charged. Input: `ticker` (path), e.g. GET /brief/KO. The first brief each UTC day is free per key and per keyless address; after that 0.25 credits. Same price as /research, a different product: brief is computed at call time from current figures; /research returns the latest written multi-analyst briefing. Data and analysis, not investment advice. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/brief/{ticker}, e.g. https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/brief/AAPL — 0.25 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 1 call(s)/day per address) Missing data? Call `request_data`.

ticker.description: US listing symbol, e.g. KO or BRK.B.
